claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

eu_status.description: The claimant's EU Settlement Scheme status, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 15 and lives with me at home. I was wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's helpful to know.

Now, let me ask you about your residency status:

**Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, there are additional criteria you need to meet to be eligible for Child Benefit.

**Which of the following applies to your current situation?**

1. You're working (earning or expecting to earn above the primary threshold for National Insurance for 3 continuous months)
2. You're looking for work
3. You have sufficient resources to support yourself financially (and don't claim Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit or Universal Credit)
4. You're studying (with sufficient resources)
5. You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national who has a right to reside

Please let me know which situation best describes you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure which one applies to me, to be honest. I haven't thought about it in those terms before.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly fine! Let me help you figure out which category you fall into by asking some simpler questions.

**Are you currently working in a paid job?** If yes, roughly how many hours per week do you work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I work full-time, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for clarifying that!

Since you work full-time, you would likely meet the requirement for people with pre-settled status who are working. Just to confirm:

**Have you been working continuously for at least 3 months, and are you earning above the National Insurance primary threshold (which is currently £242 per week or about £1,048 per month)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Honestly, I'm not entirely sure about those specific thresholds or exactly how long I've been working continuously. I just know I work full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's completely understandable - not everyone knows the specific thresholds off the top of their head.

Let me ask it in a simpler way:

**Are you employed and paying National Insurance contributions through your job?** (This would typically show on your payslip if you have one.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that either - I don't have those details to hand right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
No problem at all - I understand you don't have those details available right now.

Let me ask about Alex to make sure I have all the information about him:

**You mentioned Alex is 15 and lives with you. Is he currently in education (like at school or college)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 15, so yes, he's still at school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Now let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you the person who is responsible for Alex - meaning you're the one who looks after him day-to-day and pays for his needs like food, clothes, and other essentials?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after him and pay for everything he needs - his food, clothes, school things, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me summarize what you've told me:

- You have one child, Alex, who is 15 years old
- Alex lives with you at home
- Alex is in school
- You are responsible for Alex and pay for his daily needs
- You live in the UK
- You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You work full-time

Based on the rules, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit for Alex since he's under 16, lives with you, you're responsible for him, and you live in the UK. 

However, because you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, you need to meet additional criteria. Specifically, if you're working, you must be earning above the National Insurance primary threshold for 3 continuous months.

Since you've indicated that you don't have the information available to confirm whether you meet the specific earnings threshold or have been paying National Insurance contributions, **I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility at this time**.

**My assessment is that your eligibility is INDETERMINATE** - you may well be eligible, but without confirmation of your earnings level and National Insurance status, I cannot definitively say whether you meet all the requirements for someone with pre-settled status.

I would recommend checking your payslips or contacting HMRC directly to discuss your specific employment situation, as they can help determine if you meet the earnings threshold requirement.
